label: D2: a1 led to S1 (common) after a rewarded trial that was not in S2
explanation: Fires only at D2 and only when the agent chose a1 and reached S1 (common transition). It is silent at D1 and GO, on every S2 arrival, and on a1 to S2 rare trials; a2 to S1 rare gives only 35 activations. Within a1 to S1 common it needs a rewarded previous trial whose reached state was not S2 (prev_state -1 means the window start). That is a rewarded-S1 streak, so it is silent after rewarded S2. Magnitude is near 1.0 on long rewarded a1 to S1 streaks and grows over consecutive such trials. It is roughly halved (about 0.4 to 0.5) when the previous trial was unrewarded, and those weaker steps are most of the misses. Magnitude tracks high model value: 75% of the mass is in the top value bin. All variables in the predicate are observed at D2. Dev results: the bare a1 to S1 common predicate gets recall 1.0, precision 0.58. Adding the rewarded, not-S2 previous trial gets F1 0.87, mass recall 0.94.

issues: The original predicate missed a systematic false-positive class: the feature switches off late in the episode. Taking the original predicate restricted to each ep_trial range (dev split), precision is 0.97-0.99 for trials 3-79. It falls to 0.715 at trial 82, 0.449 at 84, 0.147 at 86 and 0.014 at 88, and is 0.0 for ep_trial >= 90 (7081 predicted steps, none active). For the ep_bucket 5 range (trials 50-99), precision is 0.697. Nearly all of the 16% false positives come from this late-episode region. The label and explanation never mention it.

The claim that the feature needs a rewarded previous trial is overstated. The hard condition is prev_state != 2. The bare a1->S1 predicate with prev_state != 2 already has recall 1.0 and F1 0.859. After ANY trial that reached S2 the feature is completely silent: 0 of 29275 dev steps fire, not only after rewarded S2 as the explanation says. A rewarded previous trial only modulates magnitude. When the previous trial was unrewarded, firing is weak and sparse (prev S1 and unrewarded: precision 0.567, recall 0.085), so the prev_reward==1 conjunct trades recall for precision rather than being a gate.

Claims that hold up: the feature fires only at D2 (zero at D1 and GO), only when S1 is shown, and essentially only after an a1 choice (a2->S1 rare gives 35 activations, precision 0.0006). The original test scores reproduce: P 0.838, R 0.888, F1 0.862.

The explanation says 'magnitude tracks high model value'. Value thresholds of 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7 do not change the predicate's scores at all, so value gives no discrimination inside the firing condition. That claim adds nothing.
skeptic.revised_label: D2: reached S1 after choosing a1 (common), when the previous trial did not reach S2; strongest after a rewarded previous trial; switches off after about episode trial 85
